0.0.n: This is the country name, linked to 観光 by の.

0.1.n: Links 日本 to 観光, describing tourism associated with Japan.

0.2.n: This noun is the subject matter that めぐる refers to.

0.3.n: Marks 観光 as what めぐる concerns; をめぐる works together as one expression.

0.4.n: Used before 状況 to describe what the situation concerns, rather than physical movement.

0.5.n: This noun is described by the preceding phrase 日本の観光をめぐる.

0.6.n: Marks the situation as the topic; the statement about it continues in the next line.

1.0.n: Before a time span, ここ indicates the recent period leading up to now.

1.1.n: 年 gives the length of the period, rather than a calendar year here.

1.2.n: Marks the time span within which the change occurred.

1.3.n: The く-form of 大きい describes the extent of the change.

1.4.n: 変化する becomes 変化しました in the polite past form.

2.0.n: 年 identifies this number as a calendar year.

2.1.n: Marks 2005年 as the time when the stated visitor count applied.

2.2.n: Added after に to highlight 2005 in contrast with later years.

2.3.n: 約 makes the figure approximate; the following 万 multiplies 670 by 10,000.

2.4.n: 万 means 10,000 and 人 counts people, so 670万人 equals 6.7 million people.

2.5.n: だっ is the part of だった that joins with た to express a past state.

2.6.n: Completes だった, the plain past form of だ; this phrase describes the following visitor count.

2.7.n: A formal compound used here to describe foreign visitors coming to Japan.

2.8.n: Combines with 人 in 外国人数 to identify the people being counted as foreigners.

2.9.n: Within 訪日外国人数, this indicates the count of foreign visitors to Japan.

2.10.n: Marks the visitor count as the topic; what happened to it follows in the next line.

3.0.n: 年 identifies this number as a calendar year.

3.1.n: Marks 2024年 as the time when the count reached the stated level.

3.2.n: Added after に to contrast the 2024 figure with the earlier one.

3.3.n: 約 signals an estimate; the following 万 multiplies 3,700 by 10,000.

3.4.n: 万 is the 10,000 unit and 人 counts people, making 3700万人 37 million people.

3.5.n: Marks the numerical level reached, not a time deadline here.

3.6.n: This is the polite past form of 達する, expressing arrival at a numerical level.

4.0.n: Introduces another development beyond the increase already described.

4.1.n: 年 identifies this number as a calendar year.

4.2.n: Marks 2025年 as the time of the expected record.

4.3.n: Added after に to make 2025 the new time frame under discussion.

4.5.n: Combines with 最多 to refer to the highest figure recorded so far.

4.6.n: With 過去, this forms an expression for the previous all-time high.

4.7.n: Marks 過去最多 as the record that 更新する will surpass.

4.8.n: 更新する literally involves renewal; with a record, it means setting a new one.

4.9.n: After a plain-form verb, 見込み expresses an expected future outcome rather than a certainty.

4.10.n: Politely ends the statement after the noun 見込み.

0.lit: As for the situation surrounding Japan's tourism,
0.tip: をめぐる before a noun means concerning or surrounding a topic, not physically going around it.

1.lit: Over these past 20 years, it greatly changed.
1.tip: ここ before a duration means the recent period up to now, rather than a physical location.

2.lit: As for the Japan-visiting foreigner count, which was approximately 670 ten-thousands of people in 2005,
2.tip: The phrase ending in だった describes the visitor count that follows it.

3.lit: In 2024, it reached up to approximately 3,700 ten-thousands of people.
3.tip: Japanese 万 groups numbers by 10,000, so 3700万 equals 37 million.

4.lit: Furthermore, in 2025, the expectation is to renew the past highest number.
4.tip: A plain-form verb followed by 見込みです expresses an expected outcome, not a guaranteed result.
